title: Does Carrying a Balance Build Credit? 🤔
description:
Uncle Ray swears you should always leave a balance on your credit card to build your score. True or false?

Part of it is true: using a card and paying on time helps your credit. But your score looks at the balance on your statement, and paying that statement in full still counts. Keep $1,000 on the card all year at about 22% APR and you pay roughly $222 in interest for zero extra points.

Verdict: mostly false. It comes down to paying the full statement balance by the due date.

Who told you this one? Tell us in the comments 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration only: $1,000 balance kept for 12 months at 22.15% APR (Federal Reserve G.19, Q2 2026 average for credit card accounts assessed interest), interest paid monthly so the balance stays at $1,000. Credit scores vary by scoring model and lender. Sources: myFICO ("You Don't Need to Carry Credit Card Balances to Improve Your FICO Scores"); Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit release, 7 Oct 2026. This is not financial advice.
